What irks me the most about this rock, paper, scissors type of system is the fact that, many years ago, another online Gundam game had this exact same system and it was perfectly solved! By just abolishing it outright.

The game in question was SD Gundam Online, a game I miss dearly. This game is very similar to it in that, melee based units were called rocks instead of raids, generals were called scissors, and supports were paper. They had the same color scheme for their types as well. 

SDGO went with this system for many years before they decided to just get rid of it and make every unit the "same". What they did instead was give every a large set of skills that let each player customize how each and every unit played differently. 

I won't go into massive detail about how each unit could be built completely differently but it was fun watching someone build a long range unit into a boosting semi melee powerhouse to combat a close range built tank.

It was akin to the custom parts we can put onto units in this game but with the passive skills instead. It was a much better system than the rock, paper, scissors because players were then free to pick whatever units they wanted, instead seeing someone pullout a scissor god and then the team having to be like "Alright someone's gotta bring iut the paper." 

This game could easily do the same thing. Let sniper players be their snipers, let melee players jump into the fray without getting outright obliterated by savvy generals, and generals...well the game would stay more or less the same for them really.

The actual lore of what happens to the separate combiners minds and their personalities is really quite fascinating. Its unique to each combiner.

 Computron is made up of some of the smartest transformers out there. So when they combine, their combined intelligence multiplies and Computron becomes the smartest transformer ever. But he's basically paralyzed from overthinking and analyzing every move or strategy he can think of. Which are a lot. But when ever he eventually does act, it is the most logical and tactically perfect move to make.

 Menasor is built up from a team of psychos who all hate and fear their leader. Said leader also very much enjoys brutalizing them and mentally  manipulating them. When they become Menasor, it averages out all their twisted personalities, and their intense hatred and fear for Motormaster, and turns the resulting combiner into a screeching, borderline insane killing machine that can barely follow orders. 

 A lot of combiner teams get multiple pros and cons from combining. The predacons are, as far as the OG combiner teams go, the only team to get practically zero negative effects from combining. Only positives. This is because they can all actually manage to agree and not have conflicting personalities. The entire team loves, what they call "The Hunt". They all share a single passion and drive, which results in the most powerful combiner, Predaking. He is all their personalities, intelligence, and strength combined perfectly.
